title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Correction Standard — Fees That Should Not Have Been Charged
content:
## Status of the opening clause

**Retired, no longer in force:** the clause that a fee which should not have been charged is reversed in full by one fee reversal referencing it has been superseded by the current Ridgeline Pro Credit basis for late fee corrections.

## Clauses in force

**Reasons for a reversal.** The reversal reason is **posting error** for:

- a late fee whose minimum was in fact covered by the due date;
- a late payment charge computed on an invoice that was in fact paid by its due date plus the tier's late charge grace days;
- a surcharge on a payment not made by bank card;
- a returned payment fee on a payment not in fact returned.

It is **dispute resolved** for a late payment charge or late fee that arose solely from an invoice later resolved in the business's favor, reversed in full when the disputed invoice was the only past-due amount.

**Owed whatever the history.** A correction is owed regardless of tier, waiver history or how long ago the fee posted, and it does not use up a courtesy waiver.

**Once only.** A fee that already has a fee reversal or a courtesy waiver referencing it cannot be reversed again.

## Points of judgement

| Situation | Reason |
|---|---|
| A bank card surcharge posted on a payment made by ACH | Posting error |
| A returned payment fee on a payment the bank paid | Posting error |
| A late payment charge arising solely from an invoice whose dispute was resolved in the business's favor, that invoice being the only past-due amount | Dispute resolved, reversed in full |
| A fee posted long ago and owed a correction, on an account that has used its courtesy waivers | Still owed; no courtesy waiver is used |

superseded_clauses: A fee that should not have been charged is reversed in full by one trade_fee_reversed row referencing it.
